builder_plan.scenario: Your coding assistant makes changes that still need substantial repair before merging.
builder_plan.change: Try the technique on held-out issues from a repository with reliable tests.
builder_plan.baseline: The same coding agent, repository snapshot, tools, and token budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct patches, regression failures, human repair time, and total cost per accepted change.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: What Does a Repair Agent Gain from Remembering Its Failure? An Exploratory Study on Real Python Bugs
summary: The technique replaces blind retry of a failed repair agent with a retry conditioned on failure memory such as the prior transcript or extracted test signals. It costs roughly one extra failed attempt's context tokens per retry, and a model-written lesson adds a further model call with no measured benefit over the raw transcript. Adoption can fail because gains were not statistically significant, outcomes varied more across bugs than across conditions, and retries shown prior test results more often broke other tests, inflating apparent gains on the bug-revealing test.
rationale: Passing the prior failure transcript into retries is cheap and API-compatible, but the evidence is exploratory and non-significant, so the reader should validate it on their own bug distribution before relying on it in production.
technique: Failure-memory retry for coding repair agents

claims.statement: The technique replaces blind retry of a failed repair agent with a retry conditioned on failure memory such as the prior transcript or extracted test signals. It costs roughly one extra failed attempt's context tokens per retry, and a model-written lesson adds a further model call with no measured benefit over the raw transcript. Adoption can fail because gains were not statistically significant, outcomes varied more across bugs than across conditions, and retries shown prior test results more often broke other tests, inflating apparent gains on the bug-revealing test.

On 75 BugsInPy bugs, retrying failed gpt-5.4-mini repairs with failure memory improved bug-revealing test pass rates by +5.5 to +9.9 percentage points over a plain retry baseline of 29.8%, but no contrast was statistically significant; a transcript beat a failure notice by +12.2 points (CI [+4.2, +20.0]) for the mini model only.
